lessons.title: Understanding Synonyms
lessons.concept: Synonyms are words with similar meanings. In aptitude tests, choose the option closest in meaning to the given word in common usage. Context matters because some words have multiple senses; pick the synonym matching the most typical meaning unless a context is given.
lessons.formula: Approach: identify meaning of target word -> compare options -> select closest meaning (consider tone/intensity).
lessons.worked_example: Word: 'Brief' — meaning short in duration or extent. A close synonym is 'Concise' or 'Short' depending on options. In general usage, 'short' matches well for duration.
mistakes: Choosing a word related by topic but not by meaning
Ignoring differences in intensity (e.g., happy vs ecstatic)
Confusing synonyms with words that merely look/sound similar

lessons.title: Understanding Antonyms
lessons.concept: Antonyms are words with opposite meanings. Determine the core meaning of the given word and select the option that expresses the opposite idea. Watch for words with prefixes (un-, in-, dis-) but verify meaning, as not all prefixed forms are true antonyms in usage.
lessons.formula: Approach: define target word -> identify opposite concept -> choose option that best represents that opposite.
lessons.worked_example: Word: 'Expand' — to increase in size/extent. Opposite idea: to make smaller. Antonym: 'Contract' or 'Shrink'.
mistakes: Selecting a negative word that is not the direct opposite in meaning
Choosing an antonym for the wrong sense of a polysemous word
Assuming a prefix always creates the correct antonym answer among options

lessons.title: Context and Degree of Meaning
lessons.concept: Synonym/antonym questions may test nuance: degree (mild/strong), connotation (positive/negative), or usage. When options are close, prefer the word that best matches meaning and intensity. Eliminate options that are unrelated or only loosely connected.
lessons.formula: Eliminate unrelated options -> compare remaining by meaning and intensity -> pick best fit.
lessons.worked_example: Word: 'Tiny' (very small). 'Small' is similar but weaker; 'Minute' can be a close synonym in sense of very small. Choose based on closest degree among options.
mistakes: Not distinguishing degree/intensity between close options
Picking a familiar word without checking precise meaning fit

practice.question: Choose the synonym of: ABUNDANT
practice.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities; plentiful. 'Plentiful' has the same meaning. The others indicate lack or small amount.
